record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Antipodal geodesics with few color changes
record.original_question: If the edges of the hypercube Q_n are colored red and blue, must there always exist a geodesic path between a pair of antipodal vertices with at most one color change? Equivalently, in every antipodal 2-coloring of the edges of Q_n, must there be a monochromatic geodesic between antipodal vertices?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1 (Leader and Long, [3]). Suppose the edges of the hypercube Qn are coloured with two colours, red and blue. Then there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most one colour-change. Equivalently, if the edges are 2-coloured ‘antipodally’ ... there exists a monochromatic geodesic path between two antipodal vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$ and whose edges connect pairs of vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Two vertices $x,y \in \{0,1\}^n$ are called antipodal if $y_i = 1 - x_i$ for every $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$. A geodesic between antipodal vertices $x$ and $\bar x$ is a path of length $n$ in $Q_n$ from $x$ to $\bar x$ (equivalently, a path that flips each coordinate exactly once). Two edges of $Q_n$ are called antipodal if they are images of one another under the antipodal map $v \mapsto \bar v$; an edge 2-coloring with colors red and blue is called antipodal if every pair of antipodal edges receives different colors.

Prove or disprove: For every $n \geq 1$ and every 2-coloring of the edges of $Q_n$ with colors red and blue, there exists a geodesic between some pair of antipodal vertices that uses at most one color change along its length. Equivalently, prove or disprove: for every $n \geq 1$ and every antipodal 2-coloring of the edges of $Q_n$, there exists a monochromatic geodesic between a pair of antipodal vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: The Leader–Long conjecture has been verified for small dimensions (n ≤ 5 by hand, and n = 6, 7 with computer assistance), and related results (e.g., Norine's antipodal-coloring conjecture, work by Feder, Dvořák, West–Wise) address variants. No general proof is known; the conjecture remains open for arbitrary n.

status_evidence.title: Maximal Monochromatic Geodesics in an Antipodal Coloring of Hypercube
status_evidence.snippet: Leader and Long conjectured that every antipodal 2-coloring of Qn contains a monochromatic antipodal geodesic; proved for small n.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture verified for small dimensions but open in general.

status_evidence.title: Antipodal monochromatic paths in hypercubes
status_evidence.snippet: For 2 ≤ k ≤ 6, every antipodal edge-coloring of Qk has a monochromatic antipodal geodesic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial verification for k up to 6.
